title: Cohort-aware temporal throttling scheme for controlled model exposure
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a cohort-aware temporal throttling layer for model rollouts that allows finer-grained control of exposure over time. The feature augments traffic-split and step schedules with a time-decay throttle and per-cohort smoothing so that sudden spikes or noisy signals from small cohorts do not trigger aggressive rollouts or premature rollbacks. Goal: reduce false-positive rollbacks and stabilize latency/cost regressions while preserving fast ramp for healthy variants.
motivation: Current step-based rollouts use fixed percentage increases and global checks. Small cohort noise (e.g., a region or customer segment) can inflate metric variance and cause unnecessary rollback cycles or slowdowns. Adding temporal smoothing and cohort weighting will improve decision fidelity and reduce operational churn for Dedicated and Private customers with heterogeneous traffic.
scope: Runtime-side throttle controller + rollout config extensions + console UI hints + e2e tests. Backwards-compatible: default behavior remains same unless throttle params specified in rollout policy. Must work with shadow probing and A/B splits and integrate with existing metric contracts and telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: New rollout policy fields accepted by API and validated by schema checks
Runtime throttle enforcer applies per-cohort time-decay to effective traffic allocation
Rollout decisions respect throttled percentages in canary step progression
Unit and integration tests covering synthetic noisy cohort signals
Dashboard shows throttled vs requested traffic and confidence band
implementation_notes: Implement as a middleware between routing policy compiler and runtime admission. Components: 1) cohort bucketer (labels + queryable attributes), 2) temporal smoother (exponential moving average with configurable half-life), 3) variance-aware adjustment (increases smoothing for low-sample cohorts), 4) override hooks for urgent rollouts. Expose parameters: half_life_seconds, min_samples, max_step_multiplier. Defaults chosen conservatively to avoid changing current customer behavior.
tradeoffs_and_risks: More complex rollout config increases surface area for misconfiguration
Over-smoothing may slow rollout of high-quality variants in stable cohorts
Cohort attribution requires enrichment from router — small latency impact to routing path
Requires careful UX to avoid confusing users about 'requested' vs 'actual' traffic
